entries.body: Trade wind sailing — yeah! We picked up wind in a squall yesterday afternoon and it has stayed with us. Last night was beautiful, flat seas, sky blazing with stars, Charlotte charging along at 7 knots. We are still going strong in 15–18 knots south winds, forward of the beam, full sails, 6–7 knots constant. Saw Athanor last night just before sunset, lost [Tenia] finally. Ran the Coconut Breakfast net this morning — interesting to see how all the boats are spread out. Just about everyone has g[one] by now.
entries.conditions: Wind: south, 15–18 knots, forward of the beam. Full sails, 6–7 knots. 24-hour run — 138 miles.

entries.body: Yesterday was a great sailing day — hit over 8 knots at times, Charlotte really charging along. Unfortunately it changed today — variable winds, lumpy seas, speed up and down. Wish it would settle in again. Life proceeds on board — schooling takes up most of the day. No time to read anymore!
entries.conditions: Variable winds, lumpy seas. 24-hour run — 143 miles.

entries.body: Got into the groove last night — 55 miles in 7 hours! Today the wind turned more [aft] so we are poled out, consequently going slower. Thomas spotted 2 whales — we got to see just the wake, going very close to the boat. Trade wind weather today — blue sky, cumulus clouds, 15–20 knots.
entries.conditions: Wind: 15–20 knots, more aft; poled out. 24-hour run — 148 miles.

entries.body: Started getting some squalls with more punch to them, finally just leaving a reef in the main for now. Could use more sun, but otherwise no complaints, we are just rolling along. Thomas caught the world's record smallest dorado today.
entries.conditions: Squally; reef in the main. 24-hour run — 148 miles.

entries.body: Good wind today, 20 knots SE, reef in all the sails, 6.5–7 knots steady. A bit boisterous for head making! Caught a tuna just before dinner last night. Thomas saw 2 pilot whales.
entries.conditions: Wind: SE, 20 knots. Reef in all sails, 6.5–7 knots. 24-hour run — 165 miles.

entries.body: The decks looked pressure washed after the torrential rains we had last night! Sails are clean too. It was no fun at the time — pole up, pole down, sails in and out. But this morning brought sunshine and calmer seas. The boys had a dinner dorado last night. There was a mayday report on the net this morning, at 4° 31.6S, 111° 48.7 W. [Bazen], [Marewa], and Athanor are diverting to check it out. We are currently sailing due west so we will be south of the position. Hope it's a false alarm! Winds are lighter today ± 10–12 ESE, making only 5+ knots.
entries.conditions: Wind: ESE, 10–12 knots, 5+ knots. 24-hour run — 136 miles.

entries.body: Yesterday afternoon we set up 4 sails — poled out genoa, staysail, main, and mizzen — got them all flying on a very broad reach, reeled off the miles all night long. Took it down this morning when the wind picked up, but it was a nice rig. Saw a small school of dolphins just after sunset — they played in the bow wave for a long time, leaping into the air and doing back flips. Today is boisterous, 20+ knots, trade wind weather, rolling. Celebrated 1/3 of the trip with a big bar of chocolate!
entries.conditions: Wind: 20+ knots, broad reach; four-sail trade-wind rig. 24-hour run — 151 miles.

entries.body: Beautiful night last night — clear, moon, stars, no squalls. Got to catch up on our sleep. Today the wind has been very light, still moving around 5 knots or less. Back to school is difficult — it takes up a lot of time.
entries.conditions: Wind: very light, 5 knots or less. 24-hour run — 142 miles.

entries.body: Cruising with our 4-sail trade wind rig again — 4 sails flying on a broad reach, 15 knots wind. Squalls slowed us down last night. Brian and I are having fun studying French. The ham radio nets are the high points of our day.
entries.conditions: Wind: 15 knots, broad reach; four-sail rig. 24-hour run — 138 miles.

entries.body: Nice night, beautiful half moon, no squalls. Today we passed the halfway point — will celebrate with spaghetti and red wine tonight. Wind light today, 10 knots, seas lumpy.
entries.conditions: Wind: 10 knots, seas lumpy. Passed the halfway point. 24-hour run — 147 miles.

entries.body: Light winds, slow going, barely 5 knots under spinnaker. But Thomas did pull in a 10-lb yellow fin tuna, so they ate well for lunch and have dinner too. Sky completely clouded over now, wind up to 10[+] reaching but still only 5–5.5. It's a peaceful day however, everyone seems content.
entries.conditions: Wind: light, up to 10 knots. Spinnaker, 5–5.5 knots. 24-hour run — 123 miles.

entries.body: Another slow but quiet night. It is very pretty at night with the moon almost full. You seem to see for miles. Kind of squally today, good sailing again, on a reach.
entries.conditions: Squally; good sailing on a reach. 24-hour run — 126 miles.

entries.body: Great night's run — some squalls, had to reef down, but still moved along. 15–20 knots of wind, Charlotte is in her element! Beam beam (broad) reaching all day under full sail. Dropped under 1000 miles to go — moral[e] has improved! Enjoyed the sunshine today.
entries.conditions: Wind: 15–20 knots, broad reach, full sail. Under 1000 miles to go. 24-hour run — 151 miles.

entries.body: It was another beautiful night with the moon so bright. Great sailing last night, 6½ knots average. Today the winds are down, still doing 5 knots with the staysail up. Sunny day, comfortable on board. Listened in to another net this morning — so many boats out here! We have finally decided to make landfall at Hiva Oa.
entries.conditions: Wind: down; 5 knots with staysail. 24-hour run — 148 miles.

entries.body: Horrible night, rolled constantly, had weird dreams. Today is sloppy and slow — wind is almost north of east. We are running dead downwind. Must expect more of the same.
entries.conditions: Wind: north of east; dead downwind. 24-hour run — 126 miles.

entries.body: Calm night, no sail maneuvers necessary. Wind turned a bit south today so we are not quite downwind anymore, less rolly. Beautiful clear skies, no clouds. We now have an ETE on the GPS — less than 100 hours!
entries.conditions: Wind: turned south. Clear skies. ETE under 100 hours. 24-hour run — 135 miles.

entries.body: Happy May Day! Sharon on Poet's Place reminisced about flowers on May Day on the net this morning. Decent night, but the wind has been dropping all day. We are still moving along at 5 knots, incredibly enough. We want to get there!
entries.conditions: Wind: dropping all day. 5 knots. 24-hour run — 135 miles.

entries.body: We just dropped under 300 miles to go. Unfortunately we still won't make it before dark on Saturday. Winds are 12–15 knots, very easterly, keep getting pushed south. Everyone else is having to tack back north to make their destination.
entries.conditions: Wind: easterly, 12–15 knots. Under 300 miles to go. 24-hour run — 133 miles.

entries.body: It was a really nice night — boat sailed smoothly, made good progress. This morning we talked to Warna Carina and Galatea on the radio and decided to change course once again. Now we are making for Nuku Hiva — we would have gotten to Hiva Oa at night. Plus the anchorage at Hiva Oa is small and uncomfortable, full of sharks. Another 60 miles, but we can make Nuku Hiva Sunday morning. We'll have to jibe as the course is now due west, impossible to steer.
entries.conditions: Course changed to Nuku Hiva. 24-hour run — 141 miles.

entries.body: This has been the longest day in the history of mankind! Moving along [in] 5 knots, feels like we are standing still. We want to get there now! Head downwind, rolling along. Nothing to do but read books and watch time pass slowly.
entries.conditions: Dead downwind, 5 knots. 24-hour run — 121 miles.

entries.body: What a wonderful 2 weeks in the Marquesas! Brian had a blast for a week with the Athanor kids — we hardly saw him. We took them all a couple of days. Started hiking up the mountain side on the road — paved switchbacks. Finally broke down and started hitchhiking. Got a ride with some locals going to collect bees. They dug a hive out of the side of a hill, smoked the bees out with coconut shell, we gorged on honey. The interior was very beautiful, different vegetation. Taiohae was one of the largest towns, were able to find some fruits and vegetables. Lots of boats in the harbor — met Dave & Gui on Galatea, great people. After Athanor left we cruised to Daniel's Bay, great landlocked harbor. Hiked to the waterfall with Galatea and Jack & Joyce from 2nd Tri. It was a magnificent walk through the valley, jagged cliffs looming over us. The waterfall was just a trickle, but Brian and I swam in the pool tucked into the rocks — kind of eerie! Daniel was a very sweet old man — gave us green coconuts to drink and we signed his book. The valley was paradise — flowers, fruit trees. The Marquesas can grow anything and the flowers are incredible — hibiscus, frangipani, bougainvillea, gardenia in a riot of colors. Also met the Japanese boat Ori Kalcum with Ken, Yuko, Yumi, Yuki on board — 12-year-old girl, very pretty, nice family, very different. We had a great time in Daniel's Bay, partied with Galatea. Then to Ua Pou and Hakahau, the main town. Visited the local museum there and learned about Marquesan history from Pascal. Then to Hakahetau, where Etienne lived. This was our favorite spot — the locals were so friendly to us. I got to practice my French — the Marquesans speak an easy version.
entries.conditions: About two weeks in the Marquesas — Taiohae (Nuku Hiva), Daniel's Bay (Hakatea), and the Ua Pou villages of Hakahau and Hakahetau.

entries.body: [Etienne] had a potluck for all the cruisers and everyone did songs or dances. Were invited to dinner by Jean-Marc, crazy Frenchman, had a wild time. Got to taste traditional Marquesan food. It was a beautiful little village. This morning they welcomed a cruise ship with singing & dancing, flower leis, food and handicrafts. Got a piece of flower stone and tou wood, both found only in Ua Pou. It was hard to leave, but the wind came back today so we are off to the Tuamotus. Idyllic stop in the Marquesas — we won't forget it. Wind SE, 15 knots, we are charging along under full sail.
entries.conditions: Departing the Marquesas for the Tuamotus. Wind: SE, 15 knots, full sail.

entries.body: Had a pleasant quiet night, steady wind but light. It got worse today! Down to less than 2 knots at times. Just set spinnaker, doing 3.3 now. Flat seas. Very comfortable on board but very hot.
entries.conditions: Wind: light, under 2 knots at times. Spinnaker, 3.3 knots. 24-hour run — 102 miles. (Expected worse the next day.)

entries.body: Well half the night was nice, under spinnaker, 3–4 knots, but of course it didn't last! Went under a cloud line at 2 am, SW winds, then no wind. Interrupted sleep, went nowhere. Total stall this morning, now we have 6 knots from the NE, under spinnaker again, 3.5 knots for a while but dropping now. Oh joy. All time slowest day!
entries.conditions: Wind: stalled, then 6 knots NE. Spinnaker, 3.5 knots. 24-hour run — 68 miles (slowest day).

entries.body: It's getting tiresome — rain & stall last night, very little wind today. We are tired of it. Now squalls from the SW, on the nose. Still too far to go. One good thing — Brian lost his last baby tooth today!!
entries.conditions: Wind: very little, then SW squalls on the nose. 24-hour run — 63 miles.

entries.body: Well calm seas don't seem so bad when you are battling 35 knots on the nose! The wind came up at 5 pm last night and kept coming. Couldn't keep the course at first. Saw a sailboat just at dusk. It was a wild night, Charlotte falling into holes, had to dump the main completely. No sleep, too rough. Wind has been letting off and backing throughout the day, sailing rather pleasantly now, reasonably upright. Didn't do anything all day but lie around and read.
entries.conditions: Wind: up to 35 knots on the nose, then easing. 24-hour run — 103 miles.

entries.body: Nice night, but the winds kept turning south. We can't hold our course today, have to motor sail to avoid hitting atolls! Hope the wind will turn more favorable this evening, we have to hang out all night and wait for the morning's slack tide. We are tired of this trip! Could sail just fine, in another direction.
entries.conditions: Wind: turning south. Motor-sailing to avoid atolls; waiting for morning slack tide.

entries.body: It was with regrets that we left Fakarava this morning — we had such a wonderful time there and made so many friends. Some of them are already in Papeete and we will see them there. Athanor stayed another week in Fakarava and the kids played together every day, exploring the motus. Infidien was there with Rick, Patty and Jessica, and we got to be friends. Then Oric Halcum came with Ken-ichi, Yuko, Yumi and Yuki and Brian played with them for a week. We met Paul & Mary on Aventura, really enjoyed them. Had 2 pot lucks on the beach. Did lots of snorkeling, drifting through the south pass. After our landfall on Sunday, May 26, we motored through the boiling cut, it was [big]
entries.conditions: About 2½ weeks at Fakarava (landfall Sunday, May 26). Anchored at the south pass near Motu Aito.

entries.body: enough to drive an armada through but still lots of current and standing waves. Then we sailed the 30 miles through the atoll to the south pass, where the other boats were anchored. Then we never moved! Diving was great — clear water, lots of groupers, black-tip sharks. Infidien let us use their dive gear to do a scuba dive and see the 'Valley of the Sharks' — 200 sharks in the center of the pass, 110' down. Best part of all was meeting Manihi & Tila at Motu Aito, their little resort. We got to be good friends — they were such easy going people. Thomas & Brian went fishing with Manihi, I had coffee with Tila. Thomas worked on their outboard and I redid their website. Tila made a fantastic 3-layer cake with peaches and custard for Brian's birthday. Aventura gave him chocolate, the Japanese gave him marbles, a necklace and fishing gear. We liked getting to know them better — Ken called me [Jill-ison]! Kids loved Brian. Tila is such a sweet person, I hated to say goodby. We had 4 great dinners over there. She gave me a carved pearl and another little thing she made herself, with coral shells and pearls. We have to go back some day — they are our family! It was a wonderful 2½ weeks. We all got to do some windsurfing. Not much boat maintenance — too much time having fun! The view was so magnificent with turquoise waters, palm trees swaying on the motus, coral and pink sand beaches! Paradise!! Now we are sailing in 15 knots, full sails, broad reach, 5.5 knots, big seas.
entries.conditions: Departing Fakarava for Tahiti. Wind: 15 knots, broad reach, 5.5 knots, big seas.

entries.body: Nice sailing, 20 knots of wind, 6+ knots, today, after a sloshy night. No problem getting to Papeete tomorrow morning. It is not uncomfortable, but we all agree sailing is boring. I'd like to write more about Fakarava. The beaches were a bit disappointing, so what looked like white sand was really coral rubble. There were some beautiful but small, pink sand beaches. Shelling was difficult, walking on the sharp uneven coral rocks, and there weren't many. The kids had fun making houses under the trees. The underwater coral was healthy, although not a lot of variety, but the fish were incredible. Some of them were almost unreal in their color variations. One especially was very shy, with lots of colors. I was the only one to see this fish! I saw an octopus which Thomas tried to spear. The unicorn fish were the only reef fish good to eat. All kinds of big groupers and snappers were undisturbed, because of ciguatera. The Napoleon wrasse was a kind of giant parrot fish with a big hump on its forehead. We got to swim with the manta rays in the pass one day. Remoras clung to the boat and came after you when you jumped in. I never tired of snorkeling and feasting my eyes on the panorama of palm trees, white coral beaches, water in varying shades of blue! Plus the friendship of Tila & Manihi. [A margin sketch of a reef fish accompanies this entry, annotated: blue patch with black bands between the eyes, orange stripe, white and gray, white and black stripes — dark colored with a horn.]
entries.conditions: Wind: 20 knots, 6+ knots. 24-hour run — 128 miles.

entries.body: What a great night of sailing! We had to slow the boat down to 5 knots — finally took the main down — so we would arrive in Tahiti at sunrise. It came slowly but we had a great landfall. Entered the harbor after sunrise, motored down to Maeva Beach, anchored near Galatea. We were happy to finally enjoy a good sail — Charlotte was going great.
entries.conditions: Landfall at Tahiti at sunrise; anchored at Maeva Beach.

entries.body: Left Moorea last night to sail to Huahine. Very boisterous conditions — confused seas, 20 knots wind, but beautiful sailing with a full moon. Thomas was cursing — it was kind of uncomfortable! Anchored at the village of Fare next to Infidien — Patty, Rick & Jessica — at 8 am. We spent little time in Papeete — rushed around buying the things we needed. The city was not thrilling — no bargains to be had, the market was disappointing. Maeva Beach was a comfortable anchorage though. Stocked up on chocolate bars & Nutella! Tuesday morning we sailed to Cook's Bay in Moorea, where we met Athanor and Oric Halcum. Cook's Bay is the most breathtaking harbor we have seen, with the cliffs towering above, rock spires with holes in the top. Took a great hike with Infidien to a lookout and some old Tahitian temple ruins, then scrambled to a [tiny] peak overlooking 2 valleys. Moorea is beautiful but too busy with tourists and lots of cars. Made a chocolate cake for Brian and had all the kids over — what a party! Saw some native dancing — girls shaking their hips, etc.
entries.conditions: About 11 days around Tahiti and Moorea — Papeete, Maeva Beach, and Cook's Bay. Wind: 20 knots, confused seas on the night sail to Huahine.

entries.body: Huahine was pleasant. The little town at the north end was nice, just real people hanging out. Brian & Thomas had a burger. Then we went to the south end with Infidien. Patty let Brian & I use the scuba gear, so I took Brian scuba diving. He enjoyed it, was totally comfortable underwater, liked having air to breathe! We walked around the south tip of the island and found an old coral block temple. Not much happening here, but peaceful. Thomas tried windsurfing, too gusty as usual. Sailed to Raiatea today, 20-some miles, light wind, downwind as usual under poled-out genoa and around the north coast of the island. Dropped the hook in deep water — 75' — near the Carenage boatyard. But first we had a close encounter with the bottom, trying to anchor near the reef. The bottom shoals extremely rapidly, from 100' to 5', and we had poor light, were on top of the sandbar before we knew what was happening. Luckily we got off without too much trouble, pushing off with the spinnaker pole while running the motor in reverse. Warna Carina is hauled out in the boatyard. Jack & Elsa, the crazy Aussies on their 3rd circumnavigation.
entries.conditions: Wind: light, downwind. Sailed Huahine to Raiatea (~20 miles); anchored in 75 feet near the Carenage.

entries.body: Light wind sail to Bora Bora. Raiatea and Tahaa were pretty and quiet, but the anchorages were too deep. We spent a while at the Carenage, bought new lifeline stanchions, checked out the local town, hitchhiked around. It was nice, but no windsurfing and no snorkeling. Sailed to the north coast of Tahaa and spent 2 nights totally alone in a small bay. The water was so calm last night the stars were reflected in it.
entries.conditions: Light wind sail toward Bora Bora. Two quiet nights alone on the north coast of Tahaa.

entries.body: Had a great time in Bora Bora — the anchorage was so beautiful. We anchored between the reef and a motu, away from town. Great snorkeling all around. The water colors were fantastic, anchored in 15 feet of water. The peaks of Bora Bora towered behind the motu! Brian got to play with Athanor and Oric Halcum kids for 4 days — they spent it all in the water. Saw a javelin throwing contest and the Bastille Day parade. 2nd Tri came in, nice to see Jack & Joyce again. Now we are on our way west — destination unsure. Spent the last week waiting for a cold front to go through, light west winds. They are south today, cannot hold the course to Rarotonga. Supposed to turn more easterly. Did get to do some windsurfing — Brian and I had fun sailing over stingrays! Saw a couple of eagle rays, several morays decorated like Marquesan tiki designs, lots of picasso fish. They are the ones I first saw in the Tuamotus.
entries.conditions: About 12 days at Bora Bora, the last week waiting for a cold front. Departing west, leaving French Polynesia. Wind: light west, turning south.
